reviews.title: Perfect for aerobics or for using under a step
reviews.text:
I was looking for a yoga mat that was thin enough to be stable under an aerobics step yet firm enough with enough give to use for shock absorption when dancing or running in place. I wasn't expecting miracles, but after reading many, many reviews, I decided to for for this one based on thinness, price, reviews of this mat and others and - what the heck - I liked the color. The one I ordered is the Turquoise Sea 4mm mat, and I paid full price for it out of my own pocket.

I was expecting to have to put the mat open in the garage for a few days, but when I pulled it out of the box and the plastic bag, it had no smell whatever. It is, indeed, quite thin - I prefer a thicker mat for poses on my knees or for doing situps on, but it's perfect for my needs. It keeps my aerobic step in place like it's glued to the floor, and it's actually really good at absorbing some of the impact when I walk or dance on it. Oh, and the color is exactly the same as it appeared on my monitor.

I expected to have to buy several mats before I found the right one, but I got lucky with this mat. I've bought a lot of things on Amazon that are okay, but for one reason or another, they are pretty meh. This mat isn't one of them. It is exactly what I wanted it to be with no smells and an attractive color. It is, indeed, sticky on the floor, and while it's too soon to see how durable it will be, it doesn't shed. And it's thin. It probably won't be enough padding if you want to spend long periods of time on your knees or doing 100 situps, but if you're actually looking for a thin mat, this 4mm one is definitely worth considering.

Once in place on my tile floor, it does not move, so the non-slip feature works well. It looks nice and provides for a clean surface to work on. The description says it is lightweight, but I'm not sure that I'd describe it that way. It's almost 3 lbs, but it does rollup into a very small package (remember, there is almost no padding). Perhaps, by lightweight, they mean that it isn't very thick? I also don't understand their reference to 'suede' in the description -- it is rubber through and through. Maybe they meant to describe it as 'suede-like' because that could make some sense -- the surface is soft and sort-of suede-like.

The material feels quite rugged and I think it'll last a long time. Once unrolled flat, it stays, and when rolled up, it maintains that shape, too. It is so very non-slip that if it is rolled and the edges aren't aligned, there is no fixing it -- usually, if the edges aren't aligned, I could tap on the edge sticking out and it would even up, but this one just stays uneven. This is not at all a problem, but if you like your roll to be even, you'll have to be careful to align the edge with each roll.

reviews.title: Great for home practice but do not roll it up!
reviews.text:
I have recently rediscovered my love of yoga and I had been looking for the perfect mat to do anywhere from 3.5 hours to 10+ hours of practice per week.

After doing hours upon hours of research, I decided to try a BMAT out. First of all, it is incredibly comfortable. Sure, it attracts hair/fur and smells like all rubber mats, but it is easy to wipe off with a damp microfiber cloth and it in no way smells toxic. I mainly leave it out in my home office/gym room and ensure it is away from sunlight, but I tried rolling it up once for a few minutes while vacuuming and regret it. There are now creases on the bottom facing part of the mat, and I would have expected better for the price. Lesson learned - I now hang it over furniture and make sure there are no folds on the mat. Regardless, I would recommend it for home practice for those who want something out of rubber and don't expect 10 years out of a rubber mat (check out other big name brands, rubber mats just fall apart over time). I look forward to at least a year of yoga on this mat, 18 months if I am lucky! This mat would cost around 25 cents per day if it lasts a year - which I think is still a good value.

reviews.text:
This mat is sold specifically for yoga, but there are multiple possibilities for its use. It is also excellent for other types of exercise such as resistance-band exercises, Pilates, and various types of core work and stretching. It can be used as a camping mat, too.

I got this mat in the "blue shadow" shade. It is a lovely, light-green color. This mat is 68 inches long, which is a similar length to a regular mattress. Like most yoga mats, it has a soft, spongy, comfortable feel. It has a bumpy, sticky texture to prevent slipping. The instructions from the manufacturer are to wipe it down with a damp cloth just before using it to further increase the stickiness. It is also easy to keep this mat clean by wiping it down regularly with a damp, soft cloth.

I own four different brands of yoga mats, and several of the mats I own are of this same Gaiam brand. It's a bit more expensive than the generic brands sold at big-box, discount stores, but it seems to be worth the extra money. Especially since, as advertised, it does not seem to have as much of a toxic smell as most yoga mats do.

This is a 5 mm thick mat, and it might not be quite thick enough for some people. Yoga mats come in various thicknesses, however, so it is possible to get a thicker mat from this same Gaiam brand if desired. If you are working out on hard concrete or ceramic-tile flooring, a 5 mm mat like this one might not be enough padding. You might want a 10 mm mat instead.

reviews.title: Great mat, very impressed with it.
reviews.text:
This seems like an excellent, well made yoga mat. Having only used it a few times it's a little tough give firm opinions on it as some of the things could go either way over the long haul. However, I like it a lot and it's currently my main mat. Here's what I've found so far:

Pros:
Better than average grip, almost too good. It can be hard to make slight adjustments, requiring you to pick up your hand/foot instead of just slide it slightly. A little annoying for transitions like Warrior 1 to Warrior 2. However, overall it's a good feature. It's still slippery when wet. So in a hot class the grip might last a little longer, but as soon as there's significant sweat, you're going to need a towel.

Good materials and construction. The bottom has a different texture than the top. They say you can use either side, but it seems like the lighter side texture is better for gripping the floor. So far I've only used it with the darker side facing up.

The mat is very thick and feels like felt. Personally, I like mats on the thicker side so I think it's great. The 'felt' feel to it worries me a little bit since it seems like it'll absorb sweat and require more cleaning than usual. So far no problem, but we'll see.

It's a bit too thick/soft to use on carpet. It's great on a hardwood floor, so when I'm in a studio it's fine. However, I occasionally practice at my house and it has carpet. A thinner mat works better for that. Not really a complaint, just a fyi, the ProSource mat is clearly designed for use on a hard floor and it works great there.

Long: 72" A requirement for me since I'm 6 feet tall.

Cons:

I'm getting used to the extra grip. As mentioned, it makes slight adjustments a bit more difficult.

It feels kind of plush. I like thick mats, so it's great, but it may not be for everyone.

The claim of TPE being 'environmentally friendly' is a bit of stretch. It's better than PVC but there seems to be mixed information about how eco-friendly it is. And trying to find a place to recycle a TPE mat is difficult. you can't just put it in the recycle bin. Something to consider if you _really_ want a eco-mat.

reviews.title: I'm so disappointed...
reviews.text:
I really really wanted to like this. There were tons of rave reviews all over the internet for this mat. In particular, countless mentions of how unbelievably sticky it is. Basically endless claims of how it's the stickiest mat they've ever felt.

I hardly ever sweat at all on my body. I am not a sweaty person. However, my hands and feet? They can get pretty wet. That being said, it's incredibly important for me to use a sticky mat to maintain Downdog and other asanas.

When I first excitedly ripped open the packaging on this mat, I was immediately smacked in the face with this incredibly strong odor.
"What IS that?!" I exclaimed.
"It smells like...fish." my mom replied while wrinkling her nose.

AND IT DOES. IT REEKED OF FISH. Those complaints about the Jade Harmony mat and the Lululemon mats smelling bad? They ain't got nothin' on this Eau de Fish. Luckily, after unrolling it on the floor and leaving it to air out overnight, the odor dissipated. So I was able to take the mat to class without smelling like a seafood market.

The surface of this mat is quite smooth, unlike the rough texture of the Jade Harmony. Though not as smooth as the smooth side of a Lululemon mat. When your hands are dry, without a doubt, the grip on this Bmat is quite good. My mother said it was much too grippy for her tastes.

I took my Bmat to an easygoing Hatha yoga class this morning and lemme tell ya. It was like a SLIP 'N SlIDE. As soon as my hands had a hint of sweat on them, they started slipping. The worst part was, when my feet started sweating as well, the sweat began to literally pool on top of the smooth mat into little mini puddles. I'm not even the type of person that drips sweat. It was purely sweat from my hands and feet. And because of the smooth surface, there was no place for the water to go. It just sat there.
I could barely even hold an asana as upright as a Warrior 2 because of how dang slippery this mat was.

Even my mom's $10 generic yoga mat that I've been using for the past few weeks felt better than this $85 (including tax) designer mat. The generic yoga mat has that rounded bumps texture that I could at least hold on to if I was sweaty. Because the Bmat is smooth, when I was sweaty, I had absolutely nothing to grip on to so I was constantly slipping.
I spent the whole class feeling so unstable I couldn't enjoy my hour of yoga practice whatsoever.

Pros:
- Made in Spain
- Pretty color
- Seems like a good company

Cons:
- Out of the box has a strong fishy smell
- Pools sweat
- Super slippery with even a hint of wetness

Even when dry, this mat is not as grippy as a Lululemon mat. I know a lot of people crap on that mat (maybe because they think the company is so overrated?) but I really think it's quite good. I loved the Jade Harmony's stickiness as well (it even ripped a couple of my hairs out on occasion), but the smell was pretty overwhelming and never really went away. It's also super heavy.

Anyway, I'm really sorry this mat didn't work out for me. I was really looking forward for this to be a winner after all the good reviews. But like all things, your mileage may vary and you don't know until you try it yourself. Back to Amazon it goes!

reviews.title: Great whey protein isolate
reviews.text:
Edit - March 2017
Fairly certain the formula changed in some way. New container of strawberry looks, mixes, and tastes differently.
Old label - Whey Isolate, Natural and artificial Chocolate Flavour, Xanthan Gum, Sucralose.
New label - Whey Isolate, Natural Strawberry Flavor, Soy Lecithin, Beet Powder, Bromelain, Sucralose.

Both of those lists are from a strawberry container. Friend uses the same product, he notices the change as well. The protein outright looks different (not nearly as pick, more towards a light orange), mixes far differently, and doesn't have as sweet of a taste.

Pros? The change makes it mix far better than it used to. Doesn't clump at all, it's not too far from MuscleTech or ON at this point.
It still tastes pretty good. It doesn't have an overwhelming strawberry taste anymore (which I will miss), but it still tastes pretty good, in some ways better.

I recently bought a few badges of MuscleTech Milk Chocolate protein, I do prefer that chocolate over Goliath's, however I don't know if the chocolate changed as well. Would definitely buy Goliath over the MuscleTech, as the Goliath is pure Isolate, compared to a mixture.

Cons? Someone asked if the formula change, seller denied any changes, just a "label update". I don't trust that. I've gone through too many containers of this protein to not notice the change.

Original - I guess I'm one of the few that don't see this protein as "too sweet". I think it's great. Taste and mixability is not as good as ON Whey Isolate, but is very close to half the price per scoop. I use a Contigo mixer bottle with a blender ball around Cintigo's mixing ball, which in combination mixes seems to anything pretty well. This protein does take quite a bit more shaking to mix it compared to any other brand I've had. I have both the chocolate and vanilla containers, friend got the strawberry. All mix great in a mixer bottle if you apply 2-3x (20-30 seconds, possibly a little more) more effort then other proteins. Would sitll highly recommend, will definitely be ordering mos

I may be a bit biased as I'm switching from a cheaper Costco's MuscleMilk protein, which is basically a bag of sweetener. After drinking that for a few months, I don't think anything will be "too sweet" for anymore.

reviews.title: really shines when used w/ a frother- makes it creamy and foamy. Nice flavor. Quite sweet
reviews.text:
It IS smooth and creamy. I get the best creaminess when I blend it with a [[ASIN:B0BBV3SLZH handheld frother like this]]. The bag doesnt specifically say creamer, and since it is a coconut powder base, --and in y experience--I wouldn't expect it to lighten coffee as much as dairy creamer. However, it can lighten it a little with a frother. Yet, if you just want it as an additive and not concerned with creaming, then know that it dissolves well with a simple stir of a spoon.

As for taste, that will come down to personal preference and perception. I am not usually impressed with flavored powders, but this is actually pleasant tasting to me. I could tell that it is "white chocolate raspberry" upon sniffing the open bag. The taste is the same. It's pretty good (to me!). Nice when I want something a little different. I have also tried it in a cup of hot cocoa with success.

Says to use 1 scoop in 6-8 ounces of coffee. I concur. I initially tried in a 4 ounce brew of espresso and that was way too sweet, but doable. Was much better in an 8-10 ounce cup.

It is quite sweet, less so when used in more liquid. Why do these products always overload with the sweetness?

Says that this container has "about 30 servings". Currently priced at $43.99 making this at best $1.47 per serving.

Is it worth it? I dont rate on price, but the LOW amount of collagen (4 grams) and MCT (1.5 grams) makes this a pricy boutique level product that doesn't offer enough of anything to make this a repurchase for me.

But the ingredients are good AND they have all these details in the product description, so it is easy enough to make an informed decision. Hence, I probably would not have ordered this had I been shopping around.

In short: taste is pretty good (can tell it is white chocolate raspberry), little sweeter than I prefer, mixes well with spoon, really shines when used with frother, nice way to get additional collagen but I wouldnt rely on it as my only source unless you are looking for low amount with a little MCT. 4 stars

reviews.title: It would be 5 stars if it tasted like chocolate...
reviews.text:
A few factors went into this review:
- Taste
- Texture
- Ingredients
- “Isolate” vs. “Concentrate”

Taste: Unfortunately, very disappointing. I was excited to see a chocolate flavor in a protein powder that touted all natural ingredients, no artificial sweeteners or preservatives, and most importantly, a whey isolate (more on that later). I was a little surprised to see how light colored the powder was. When blended up into a smoothie, it is difficult to tell that you used a chocolate vs. a vanilla powder. I gave it the benefit of the doubt, and tasted it. It literally has no chocolate taste. Putting a dab of the powder directly on your tongue has a slightly stronger chocolate taste, but it’s extremely mild. Perhaps it’s a very weak concentration of cocoa powder to the rest of the ingredients, but this is the primary reason for the low rating. I had been really looking forward to a nice rich chocolate taste for my smoothies for something different.

Texture: High marks on texture. The powder blends nicely, and very smoothly and evenly. No grittiness and nothing left on the sides of my nutribullet container. I made a smoothie that I drank throughout the day and it stayed evenly blended (some powders seem to ‘reclump’ fairly quickly, which is a real pain).

Ingredients: Antibiotic & hormone free, non-GMO. I’m presuming this refers to the milk that comprises the whey that makes up the actual protein powder. As a family we consume only antibiotic and hormone free dairy products so it’s really great to find more and more protein supplements that are committed to using milk from cows raised with this ethos as well.

Isolate vs. Concentrate: We have a family member who is lactose intolerant. Most protein powders are ‘whey protein concentrate’ (meaning there is lactose present). Whey is the liquid portion of the milk that separates from curds during the process of making cheese. It contains protein, fat, carbs, vitamins and minerals. In terms of protein powder, it is easily absorbable and has been shown to boost ‘glutathione’ (GSH) an important and water-soluble antioxidant. It is also extremely high in amino acids. Whey protein ISOLATE means that the producer further processes the product to remove the lactose from the whey.

The bottom line: If the taste were more chocolately, I would be more satisfied. It is a great product otherwise with the natural ingredients and the isolate vs. concentrate if you have lactose intolerance or are on a FODMAP diet, etc. It is a very large container of powder and will last a long time.

* I received the powder for evaluation and review

reviews.title: Good Quality
reviews.text:
I have been using Legion's products for a while (mostly Pulse and Recharge), but I had never ventured into buying their Whey Protein. I had been using other products, but finally decided to test it out.

All of Legion's items are high quality products you can trust. In the past, I have tried different flavors, but I really wanted to get unflavored whey protein powder so that I could decide to flavor my shake however I wanted to without an overpowering flavor. Besides the fact that it is non-GMO and hormone/antibiotic free, it is from grass-fed cows. What I also liked about the ingredients of the protein powder is that there are no added sugars and only 1g of total sugars, whereas others protein powders I have used in the past have had anywhere from 1.5g - 2g sugar per serving. There is also 25g of whey protein isolate per serving, which is pretty good. Also, when you compare calories, this was also the lower in caloric intake by 10-20%.

When I first opened the bottle, I was surprised to see that it was only 60-70% full. It was really strange; seemed like a waste of money on the packaging. Why not make the bottle smaller? Then, I looked at the net weight on the packaging. It was only 1.75 lbs, whereas it had been advertised as 2 lb. Guess they decided to round up. I looked at Legion's other flavors and realized that some of Legion's protein powders are 2 lb and others are only 1.75 lb. Not sure why they felt they needed to reduce the quantity of this one by 12%. Not a huge deal, but if you are comparing costs between this protein powder and others, take note on the amount of protein powder you are actually buying.

I tried this mixed with water and also with some almond milk. In both cases, it mixed in with the liquid pretty easily. With the water, there was a subtle taste, but not too noticeable. When mixed with almond milk, I can barely perceive a difference in the taste.

Overall, good quality product with good amount of protein and without an overpowering flavor.

reviews.text:
I bought the Promix casein on sale on Prime Day. Its flavor is fantastic—a very natural dark chocolate type of flavor. If you like dark chocolate, you'll like this. It isn't sweet enough for my tastes, so I add a bit of stevia when I make my shakes and I end up with a wonderful bittersweet concoction. Sometimes I add a tablespoon of almond or peanut butter if I haven't eaten enough fat for the day.

Performance wise, I don't notice any real difference between this and other brands of casein. I'm a personal trainer and I train six days a week, mostly for hypertrophy and strength—powerbuilding, one could say.

Flavor aside, protein supplements are, for the most part, interchangeable. Your body is going to take the proteins, break them into the constiuent amino acids, and reassemble them into muscle tissue. That being said, the ingredient list of Promix is fairly clean and contains fewer ingredients than most, which is nice. For people frightened by ingredients with too many syllables, this will be a plus.

In my opinion, this protein is not worth $90 for 5 pounds which is the price at time of writing—for unflavored, no less. I paid about $58 on prime day, but IMO around $70 would be a fair price for the 5 lb chocolate tub.

reviews.title: Middle of the road powder, blueberry is so-so
reviews.text:
So I am slowly working my way through every protein powder sold on Amazon, at least sold in 3lb+ tubs, just to get a sense of what's out there. Been doing it for almost ten years now. I have just one scoop, six days a week, usually w/ 5g creatine and ~10g psyllium husk fiber. I don't have a lot of mass, I'm ~5'10 and 183, not a body builder, just staying fit.

This powder - Maxler 100% Golden Whey Protein - is solidly middle-of-the-road. Decent protein content, no protein bitterness, no gastrointestinal issues, okay consistency. I've had better, I usually say Isopure Zero is my preferred supplement, but if you just want a decent protein powder for maintaining bulk, this is probably a good choice. This sort of powder will smell if you don't wash your shaker well, so be sure to do so, and give it a spray of rubbing alcohol, both the cap and the cup. Should keep things clean.

Flavor-wise - this is the first time I've ever purchased a fruit-flavored powder, I went for the blueberry because, you know, YOLO and all that. It is as expected - synthetic and overly sweet. I don't hate it, I intend on finishing the powder, but I don't think I'd recommend it either. Just basic vanilla or chocolate seem to be the best way to go, at least for me.

So would recommend as a decent maintenance powder.

reviews.title: Great tasting product. No stevia or monk fruit!
reviews.text:
I bought this since I am trying to lose weight. Replacing 1 - 2 meals a day with protein drink. Whey Protien products I did not like (have some lactose issues), so I tried Pea Protien. It fills me up and satisfies my appetite. Trying to find one without artificial sweeteners, stevia or monkfruit has been a challenge and time consuming. So this was a good find!

Carmel Toffee flavor is light but tasty. Dark Chocolate is very good ... my favorite! Vanilla is light ... but good. All 3 of these are perfect for a breakfast coffee or espresso smoothie. I use my blendjet with 8oz milk, almond milk, oat milk or coconut milk, add 1 heaping tsp instant coffee or espresso powder, 1/2 frozen banana, 2 scoops Vega Made Simple Vanilla, Carmel Toffee, or Dark Chocolate. The dark chocolate is good without any added sweeteners. Then add ice to the top and if needed top with 1 tsp of 100% Maple Syrup, Agave or honey ... Blend and enjoy!!!

Vanilla can also be mixed with other frozen fruits like mangos, peaches, Strawberries, blueberries, and bananas. Add Greek Yogurt for a special treat.

It will settle to the bottom some if you let it sit very long. That's why I like using my personal BlendJet blender. A shaker bottle would also help to keep it mixed if you can't drink it right away.

The only flavor I wasn’t fond of was the Strawberry Banana. It had citric acid added so it was to acidic for me. It reminded me of fruit flavored cereal I had as a kid growing up. I also tried it with a half frozen banana and a few frozen strawberries to help thicken it more like a shake. It was much better tasting, but would probably be just as good with the Vanilla as a base.

Overall I like this product. No Stevia, Monk Fruit or artificial sweeteners. I will be buying more in the bigger size containers.

reviews.title: My take on the vanilla
reviews.text:
I bought Muscle Feast Grass Fed Whey Protein Isolate because I was looking for grass fed isolate from cows not treated with hormones, and this fit the bill. There were a lot of positive reviews, but I did notice some newer reviews talked about a change to the formula that made it too sweet.

So here's my take, as a person who's used a lot of whey isolate products. The vanilla Muscle Feast protein powder mixes as well as any powder with relatively few ingredients, which is to say not quite as well as those with additional ingredients, but that's okay - I wanted less ingredients, more protein. The stevia taste is very strong and overwhelms with its sweet/bitter taste.

As a very regular stevia user, I know what I consider too much stevia, and this was definitely want over the line off too much. But here's what I did about it. For every 20 grams of powder, I add a slightly heaping teaspoon of unsweetened cocoa powder, which really takes the edge off. And sometimes a teaspoon of light sour cream, as well. And suddenly the protein drink is much more pleasant, even enjoyable. I tried a vanilla powder product, but I didn't like the end result as much. Still, if you have one you like, I'd say it's worth a shot.

I talked to a very courteous Muscle Feast rep about the overwhelming stevia taste, and that rep said that some people had complained that the powder wasn't sweet enough. They said that some users mix half unflavored powder and half vanilla, but that would also get rid of the vanilla taste, which (for me) works very well with the cocoa powder.

One other thing I wanted to point out is that Muscle Feast doesn't put certain information or icons on their powder to inform potential users. For example, if you look at the questions on the product page, you'll discover that the milk is sourced from Germany. You won't, however, find that into on the bottle. And while the find print of a longish paragraph on the bottle says this product is undenatured, it's not shown on the bottle in a way that stands out.

WIth my cocoa powder tweak, I'm happy with Muscle Feast Grass Fed Whey Protein Isolate, and I've ordered some unflavored to add to pancakes and breads. It's nice that there's a product for a reasonable price that hits all my wants for a protein powder. My previous favorite is about $50 for 2 pounds (Opportuniteas), and their chocolate has sugar (I'm diabetic, so staying away from sugar), so Muscle Feast's price for 2 pounds is definitely wallet-friendlier.

reviews.text:
I really like this! I have the flavored (turmeric) option, and it is better than expected. When I see powdered "bone broth", I basically expect zero flavor (which is fine as it is the collagen I am after), but this flavored variety isn't just a "flavored" plain powder, it actually tastes like broth. Take a look at the ingredient list in their product picture, and you will see that it has a soup broth tasting vibe to it.

NOTE ON COLLAGEN. The "beef broth propriety blend" states that is has 12.9 grams. Within this blend there is collagen. You may be wondering how much exactly. Little trick: collagen and protein have a near 1:1 ratio. The protein has to be listed separately on a nutrition label. This label says it has 7 grams of protein per serving, SO given this, you will know that there is 7-8 grams of collagen per serving.

The directions say to use 1 scoop in hot or warm water, but not how much water. I assumed 8 ounces, and I think that is accurate. I used two scoops in a 16 ounce mason jar (maybe filled 14 ounces of water), and that tasted very nice. I drank it as is, but it would work great with some added protein, noodles, veggies, etc added in. Could add to other broth, or whatever.

4.5 stars, but making it 5 because I like it more than 4 (and we cant do half stars). ALSO, I just added another tub to my cart so that says somethinbg. The current 30% coupon makes it more reasonably priced than the $29 price tag

reviews.title: I Bought This Direct From Stores - One Can at a Time - Back When One COULD Do That
reviews.text:
I bought this direct from health food stores in Idaho. It tasted good. I became loyal. Then, it stopped being available in stores. Then, I started buying it by mail direct from Lewis Labs. THEN, the company started making the minimum purchase two cans, which discriminates against the single and childfree.

When I called Lewis Labs, the phone call would not even be put through unless the number showed on their caller ID. What, a heavy breather is gonna call and start saying vulgar sweet nothings to a brewer's yeast seller?!?

"But wait, there's more!"

THEN, the company seemed to stop making nutritional "yeast". It started selling, again online direct, "yeast flakes" and "yeast buds".

Not only could I not buy ONE can of nutritional yeast, but would have to buy two cans and pay more postage, but couldn't even get brewer's "yeast".

What's next -- yeast goldfish, yeast angels and yeast tiny hearts?

Finally, the inevitable: loyalty to a brand destroyed by the brand itself.

After a decade of loyalty, I've been outta there almost another decade.

reviews.title: Stuck with a 5lb container?
reviews.text:
Got carried away and bought this and the weight gainer. Does it work? Yes. Gained 5 lbs in a matter of weeks. But alot of it was bloating as well. Read on.

Ive tried the other similar highly popular brand. Cant say this is better or worse. I do know that both makes me fatigued, nauseous, bloated and itchy. I dont think it has to do with the quality of the whey itself. Im sure they source from good places. That being said, I am more sensitive than most people and am acutely aware how something affects my body since I dont drink, smoke or do any drugs- prescribed or illegal.

The essential problem I believe lies in the processing. I never have issues eating whole unprocessed foods. I can eat lots of good quality chicken and beef without any adverse health symptoms.

Whenever something gets processed, something goes wrong. You may want to ask yourself how they create these fine powdered substances through machines. Then ask how do they maintain and clean these machines, especially small crevices and areas where it becomes very difficult and time consuming to do so. Then ask yourself do they do it enough. Is it possible that it goes without cleaning for days and weeks on end? Even if its cleaned frequently enough, is it sufficient enough? Do they hit all the cracks and crevices? Have you seen what old food processing machines look like even after being cleaned?

If it not the process, then my assumption that the source is of high quality is wrong.

So what do you do if you are like me, and you are stuck with 5 pounds of powder that you have difficulty stomaching and you don’t want to just trash it since you can’t return it? Dont take more than once a day. I would take half the normal or even a quarter of the normal dose and slowly finish the bag/container. Then make sure you eat a whole banana or fruits and on top of that take a quality multivitamin and then extra vitamin B. Do not use a mixer. Chew like our ancestors did. This detox will help flush out the invisible toxins in the powder. Once you are done, never look back and stick to whole foods. Your body will work less hard by not having to deal with/fight off toxic elements. We have enough to deal with, we dont need to ingest them if we dont have to.

reviews.title: Not a bad powder
reviews.text:
I had gastric bypass almost 5 years ago and I am always looking for ways to help supplement my protein intake. I saw this powder and decided to give the chocolate a try.

Pros: I love the individual packets. I love the nutritional value since I am supposed to stay low carb and low sugar.

I threw in a pack with some water and shook it as directed. It blended well, there were not any clumps (Which you tend to get if the liquid is too warm, keep it below 140 degrees F people).

My first sip was a bit meh. Second sip was actually pretty decent. It does taste a bit too sugary for me, but that could just be how my tastes have changed since my surgery.

The powder was packed well, it was in a vacuumed sealed bag, which I suspect was done to fix some of the other issues I was reading about for example the packets sticking together, etc.

All in all it is a pretty decent protein powder. I did not feel sick drinking it, which tends to happen with me and powders. It was a decent chocolate flavor, and I think the next time I drink this I will try using milk of some sort to see if that cuts down on the sugary taste for me.

reviews.title: Wow - best tasting powder yet!  Vanilla Ice Cream flavor
reviews.text:
Well, I've been trying out various protein powders this year, for trying to lose weight, not for working out.
As I type this, I have six different brands in house in various flavors. Syntha-6 beats them all on the flavor.

I try the mixes with milk, but judge them on how I normally drink them, which is with cold water.
(Milk and I don't agree very much, so I have to limit my milk intake drastically.)

So far, I've only tried the Syntha-6 in the Vanilla Ice Cream flavor. I read through almost all the reviews before purchasing,and looked up more on the actual contents of the product on another site. (This is a downfall of Amazon's - they don't provide enough information on the ingredients for food products! To list foods, I wish they'd require at minimum that the Nutrition Facts label contents be posted!

Anyway, I must say that this powder has fantastic flavor, both with water and with milk. It is higher in calories than some of the other brands out there, but has more protein. One of the reasons I tried it (and the reason I rule out many other brands/flavors) is that this has NO ASPARTAME. I am allergic to it, and must watch all foods and supplements carefully for it being snuck in to the mixes. This does have some corn syrup in it, which is probably why it tastes so good! But, if you are someone who is avoiding corn sweeteners, then note that this item has it.

It tastes a lot like a bowl of good vanilla ice cream that melted would taste. Yes, it is that creamy and tasty.
My only real complaint about this item is that it makes a very thin-bodied shake. It is like a glass of vanilla milk
in texture. If you mix it with water, it looks like really cheap skim milk. That's a bit of a put-off. I ended up mixing it half and half with a flavor of Spiru-Tein and got a decent, tasty thick shake. (Note that I really don't like Spiru-tein's vanillas - there's not much hope for them. But other flavors mix nicely with this brand's vanilla.)

Now, note that I have limitations in my mixing that many others won't have. I am partially disabled, so can't always get ice when I want it, or just throw some frozen fruit into the mix. Many times, I am home alone and the kitchen is downstairs, out of my reach. I did try this with ice, and that helped A LOT. Definitely better and a tad thicker when ice cubes were added to the mix. But, I don't see why Syntha-6 doesn't add a little more of some type of thickener to the mix. It would make a world of difference in the general texture of the drink. I haven't tried adding a little guar gum myself yet, so don't know if that would help.

Here is the ingredient list:
A Sustained Release Ultra-Premium Protein Matrix Comprised of (Ultrafiltered Whey Protein Concentrate [Milk] Rich in Alpha-Lactalbumin, Microfiltered Whey Protein Isolate [Milk] Rich in Whey Isolate Peptide Fractions, Calcium Caseinate, Micellar Alpha and Beta Caseins and Caseinates [Milk], Milk Protein Isolate [Milk], and Egg Albumen [Egg], Glutamine Peptides), Richmix Sunflower Powder Consisting of (Sunflower Oil, Corn Syrup Solids, Sodium Caseinate [Milk], Mono- and Di-Glycerides, and Dipotassium Phosphate), Litesse II Polydextrose, Natural and Artificial Flavors, Nutrisperse MCT Powder Consisting of (Medium Chain Triglycerides, Non-Fat Dry Milk, Disodium Phosphate, and Silicon Dioxide), Ticalose Cellulose Gum, Sucralose, Acesulfame Potassium, Lecithin [Soy], Aminogen, and Papain.

Overall, I really like this product. Since I started using it, my nails have been growing like crazy! Not sure if it is related to this product, but it was certainly a change I experienced. I don't feel hungry afterwards, and it doesn't leave me with "hairy tongue" like some powders do. I definitely will be trying some other flavors as the finances allow.

reviews.title: Good tasting and organic, but very expensive
reviews.text:
I’ve been using protein powder for over two decades, everything from the macro brands to the Boutique brands. This one tastes quite good and dissolves well in water. It dissolves so so in milk, so use a shaker bottle with a whisk ball and you’ll be fine. Expect some foam with milk, so you’ll have to let it settle unless you like foam. I don’t.

I really appreciate the organic everything here, but danged it’s expensive for the amount you get. And it’s concentrate at that. Nothing wrong with whey concentrate unless you’re lactose intolerant or on a serious cut, but damned, this is too expensive. Did I already say that? I guess I did and said it again, because that’s the bitter aftertaste with this.

It has a good protein to calories ratio for concentrate.

I give this five stars for quality, four on taste, and four stars overall because I have to detract something for the price and packaging since it’s the overall product I’m evaluating here. At the current price of over seventy dollars for two pounds though, I would look elsewhere and will be doing so. If money is no object though, it’s good stuff as long as it suits your needs and you can fit it into your macros.

reviews.title: It's Delicious but It Makes me Gassy later in the Day.
reviews.text:
I bought the Food Chocolate Caramel from my local store. It's is delicious and easy to blend in my Ninja or blender shake bottle. I LOVE that it's a meal replacement and it works great since I don't get hungry at all until lunch. ( I have this shake every AM for breakfast.) I also have JJ Virgin's Paleo-inspired protein powder but although I love that too, it doesn't cause any gas. On the same token, it doesn't keep me satisfied or full so I get hungry around 2-3 hours after consuming her product.
I reiterate that I love the Phood Chocolate Caramel because of the ingredients, all vegan, no artificial sugars, etc. My only complaint is it makes me gassy starting around early evenings. I've done "tests" on this by totally skipping it for a few days and just having a different shake (mentioned above). And I don't have gas problems at all. Then I consumed the Phood protein at another time and again, I'd get gassy later on in the day.
I prefer this product (Phood) because it keeps me feeling less hungry longer and as another reviewer mentioned, I'm also not tired and feel energized. Is it me or is anyone else notice they get gassy from this product? And to add a note: Although I experience gas with this product, I love the PROS more than the con (gas only) so I purchased my 2nd container. If it doesn't affect you with gassy stomach later on during the day, this is good stuff, satisfying and to me delicious.

Has artificially made ingredients – sucralose most concerning

The bag
The powder arrived in a 9” inch tall, 5½” wide and near 2 ½” deep sealed plastic like food type bag that the top can be torn off and then allowed to reseal, with no issue.

Aroma & Taste
There is no accounting for smell or taste, however, chocolate is universal, and this has a mild, delicate aroma and taste of a chocolate (water based) shake.

The Great Debate
The science is kind of thin surrounding the benefits of these kinds of supplements, however, it’s universally known that cultures with heavily biased protein-based diets may grow taller. Now whether there are health benefits using this product will not be outlined or debated here, as the reader can make that conclusion independently. Notwithstanding, this writer wanted to take advantage of those benefits we understand are associated with taking this supplement which is marketed toward growth in height for children.

Value
This offers pricing that is competitive with other supplements that have some, but not all the same ingredients. These powders never seem to be inexpensive. There is a price to pay for results, I guess. I have never seen such vitamins and minerals targeted so specifically for children and their growth, so this is where the value seems to come into play. I am happy to have selected this to at least try, the results are still pending, as any results are measured in months, not days.

The Brand
I never heard of the TrueHeight brand before selecting this.

GMP
This was reported to have been made using GMP (good manufacturing practices).

Allergy Warnings
This was manufactured in a facility that processes milk, eggs, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, soy and wheat, and that those ingredients may be in this powder.

The powder
The powder is very soft. The texture is smooth. The powder, with enough mixing, for the most part, dissolved in water in a fairly short time. The powder did not clump, like a rock, in the bag or in the liquid.

Ingredients
The powder is made in the USA, from globally sourced ingredients. We would suggest reading the label on the bag in the listing, however, that listing’s picture is different from what we received. I’m not happy about that. Either have the formula down pat or not, but I do not like to be part of any experiment in formulation, and for that reason, a star is taken away.

Artificial sweetener
Has artificially made ingredients – sucralose most concerning. I will leave that to the reader to decide whether they want something that science had to create to make.

Best of both worlds
These have the best of both worlds, vitamins and minerals and a formula for growth. So, we can say goodbye to chewing or swallowing a hard pill that’s even close to these ingredients. I think this should be beneficial, only time will tell, and in this instance, I was given a bag with (15) servings, which is not going to last the many months needed to see results.

Digestion
No complaints if taken during or just after a meal.

Fresh product received
The date of manufacture was labeled. October 05, 2022, I received these at the start of December 2022. Expiration was labeled as being September 2024.

Always consult a healthcare professional prior to anyone taking a supplement.

I hope my thoughts were informative.

reviews.title: Great taste! Some unnecessary fillers
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Easy to Drink and Sweetened Artificially
reviews.text:

The ingredient label on my package looked slightly different than the listing as it contained not one, but two artificial sweeteners. It uses Acesulfame Potassium and Sucralose for sweetness. If you are ok with that, it’s easy to drink and contains a good amount of protein.

reviews.title: Not Easy to Dissolve/ Difficult to Seal Ziplock
reviews.text:
This is the third product I have tried from Bulk Supplements, and like all their other products, the ziplock on the bag can be difficult to completely seal. It also would have been nice if the ziplock was sealed during shipping. I had to carefully shake and squeeze the bag in order to avoid spilling protein while I was tearing it open. Sealing the ziplock would have prevented the protein from getting up around wear the bag is torn open.

As for the protein itself, the only difficulty I experienced with it was how it dissolves. I expected to be able to add a couple scoops to my normal whey protein shake to add more of a diverse protein profile, but the casein does not dissolve nearly as easily. I tried mixing with two kinds of shaker cups, and it made no difference. There will be small chunks if you use a shaker, and you will need a little more liquid. I've yet to try a blender, but I imagine that would be the best way to mix the protein.

Overall, I don't think the protein is bad, I just think it's use would be best served for those who use a blender to make their protein shakes or to add it to a smoothie or something.

reviews.title: Low-carb flour- great for crackers, pizza crusts, soft tortillas, pita breads, biscuits..
reviews.text:
I've used 2 different organic pumpkin seed flours on Amazon.. this one and one other..
Differences I noticed is: the other brand said it was a 'product of China' while this brand said they are made from pumpkin seeds 'native to Central America' .. also this brand said that they use an 'age-old cold-pressing process' to naturally remove some of the seeds oil thus concentrating the protein.. the other brand didn't mention doing that. There is a difference price wise also with this one costing more than the other when u compare the amount you receive for the price.

We bought this for my husband who has been doing a low-carb keto diet ... this pumpkin seed flour has very low carbs (when u subtract the fiber)!! So we have used this to make crackers, pizza crusts, soft tortillas, pita breads and biscuits!! .. He loves it and can eat and not feel like he's missing out .. I will share our cracker recipe for anyone who wants to try it. We've also used other low carb flour (like almond and peanut) but now that we've found pumpkin seed flour which is very low carbs he prefers it.. I do wish it cost less..

My Italian cracker recipe:
1/2 cup pumpkin seed flour
1 tbsp Italian seasoning
1 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp onion powder
1 tsp oregano seasoning
1/4 tsp sea salt or to desired taste
2 tbsp olive oil
2 'chia eggs'*

Directions:
Preheat oven to 350'.. Mix all dry ingredients thoroughly... I use a fork to make sure its pressed and mixed well.. then add olive oil and mix thoroughly until it looks crumbly. Next add the 'chia egg' mixing well.. it maybe slightly wet & sticky but that's ok. Put the doughty ball on parchment paper and add another sheet of parchment paper on top.. press down and then roll it out to your desired cracker thickness. Then cut into squares and possibly sprinkle a touch more sea salt if you like more salt. Bake 15-20 minutes or until crispy.. oven temps vary so check around 15 minutes to make sure not burning. Enjoy!! ;)

*chia egg- Mix 1 tbsp of ground chia seeds with 3 tablespoons of water. Since this recipe calls for 2 chia eggs u would mix 2 tbsp of ground chia seeds with 6 tbsp of water.

**also on a side note I've read online that pumpkin seeds are known to remove intestinal worms ...

I shared a pic of the low carb crackers & cheese biscuits that I make with this flour .. I will try to add my cheese biscuits recipe soon! :)

reviews.title: Indigestion
reviews.text: Xantham gum is a thickening agent used in a lot of protein powders. It will often cause indigestion. When mixing the product in water, I could tell the powder had a significant amount of xantham gum based on how thick the drink became. I assume it’s this ingredient causing very painful IBS symptoms. I’ve had many different protein powders and this one by far causes the most digestive issues. If you’re a serious lifter looking to pack on muscle, you’re going to be ingesting a couple scoops a day which can cause major irritability. If you’re not sensitive to xantham gum then you should be fine.

reviews.title: Excellent Whey
reviews.text:
I've had some issues with Whey in the past. Sometimes it has a really funky taste or it doesn't blend well. Thankfully this one doesn't have a funky taste and it blends perfectly.

FLAVOR

So first I should say that I never drink / eat this stuff by itself. I've always mixed Whey into something else. That being said, this adds a slight vanilla flavor that is pretty nice and combines with other things well. I actually combine it with frozen fruit (pineapple is one of the best) and coconut milk. That makes an excellent smoothie.

CONSISTANCY

Like I said, this blends in really well. At no point have I ended up with chunks of powder or any kind of grittiness.

REACTION

I put this one in here because I've tried some powders that upset my stomach a little or left me feeling off. This one doesn't do that to me. I feel find after consuming it.

This is one of the best Wheys I've tried. However there are others that are just as good. If you have one of you like and it's the same price or cheaper, stick with it. If this one is cheaper, go for it. You won't be disappointed.

reviews.title: Good taste and good for my (basic) needs
reviews.text:
Taking my effort to get healthier a little more seriously, and I want to make sure I'm fueling my body correctly. I'm not a body builder nor am I a serious athlete, I'm a mom who wants to better herself for her long term health and family. With that being said, I'm not anal retentive about my supplements, as long as they are decent quality.

With 25g of protein and a supplement that promotes lean growth and helps with recovery it checks the minimal boxes that I have. After my morning workout after dropping off the kiddos I add oat milk, a banana, and a scoop of this into a personal blender bottle and add some ice. Once it's all blended I down it while I start planning for my workday. I'm a bit of a creature of habit so the format I just described is my daily routine and the only way I use this. With the oat milk and banana and ice it makes a great tasting morning meal -- the vanilla toffee is not overpowering and adds a nice depth to the flavor. This also keeps me satisfied from a hunger perspective. Overall, I'm very satisfied with the product and the taste. It meets my needs.

reviews.title: Ion Exchange method of processing === BAD!!!
reviews.text:
Look for CFM (Cross-flow Microfiltration) for your protein isolate. It costs more but is worth every penny.
Why?

Because:

"The problem with Ion-exchange processing is that they are made by running concentrates through what is called an ion exchange column, which separates proteins based on their electrical charge, which then alters the pH of the whey. Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide are the chemical reagents normally used to achieve this. The electrical charge on the proteins attaches them to resins in the reaction vessel. Obviously, these reagents damage pH-sensitive fractions and denature some amino acids. It becomes clear that we can say goodbye to glycomacropeptides, the immunoglobulins, lactoferrin, the growth factors, and a big percentage of the alpha-lactalbumin content. Cysteine and methionine will also be denatured (lost)" -- KAHA

reviews.title: Awesome quality, hefty price
reviews.text:
An incredible ratio of protein per serving. Each scoop is nearly all protein. You can compare it to your regular protein by looking at the grams of protein per serving and then looking at the total grams per serving. So if it has 20 grams of protein in a 25 gram scoop, you have 80% protein, 20% everything else, usually carbs/sugars. This has the best protein ratio I've used. And I've used dozens of protein powders.

The Taste - Nonexistent. I was stunned when I tasted this stuff. I have never tasted an "unflavored" powder and actually agreed with using this label. This one I do. There is some sort of taste besides water, but it is so subtle I don't mind it much at all. Now, if you are used to high sugary, cookie chip filled garbage protein shakes, this is going to taste horrible to you. But for me, I thought it was easy to drink without choking.

The results - I haven't finished the entire bag yet, so I can't emphatically claim any concrete results. But I definitely believe I will continue getting good if not even better results because of the purity of this formula. If it turns out otherwise, I will definitely update this review.

The price - Too much. I know others have stated the price is fine for them. They must not use protein powders to the level I do. I usually spend around 40$ for 5 pounds of powder. This one is the same price for 2 lbs. That is quite a difference. I freely admit that when you add up price per gram of protein, it is not as bad, but it is still difficult for me to shell out this much so often. If they could get the price down closer to the competitors, I would not just be a committed customer, but an evangelist for this brand. We will see.
Overall, I really like this brand and will keep it on my radar. If the price comes down a bit, it will be a regular part of my rotation.

reviews.title: The shampoo itself is great, but beware this seller.
reviews.text:
I've used Aveda's Scalp Benefits shampoo for years now...and I love it...but I also know what the product ought to be and what it shouldn't be.

Beware of this particular seller. For some reason, the shampoo I purchased from this seller came very thinned out and opaque; as if watered down with something sort of milky. The top of the shampoo separated from the bottom, and it wasn't that wonderful, thick, luscious, clearish gel you usually get with Aveda...when I tipped the bottle over (cap still closed of course), the air bubble at the top went all the way to the other side in no time, and when I poured it out on my hand to use it, it was thin for Aveda.

I don't know if the product was tampered with, put in inappropriate temperatures, or what happened to it. I ended up having to drive to the Aveda store (about an hour away). I tried to exchange the product there and they wouldn't, because this was from a different seller. This was supposed to be a gift for someone, but I ended up having to buy an additional bottle from the store itself since they wouldn't exchange it, and I needed the shampoo. At the store, I can at least tell what the viscosity is because I can tilt the bottles in the store to see that it's correct.

In the photo, on the left, is the bottle from "Elizabeth Adam Day Spa"(the seller), and ton the right is what is left over from my current supply, the bottle I bought I gifted. But notice that on the right, that one is clear. On the left, that bottle only has clear stuff at the bottom. The rest of it is sort of thin and kind of milky. It's weird.

reviews.title: My first experience with a shampoo bar
reviews.text:
I've been curious about shampoo bars for quite some time. They are great to add to emergency or travel bags, and I wanted to know if it would be a product I could use. The sulfate-free, paraben-free, cruelty-free, and phthalate-free benefits are excellent. The shampoo bar arrived in a thin box that can be tossed into the recycling bin. It is wrapped lightly with tissue paper. I could smell the bar as soon as I opened my package. It is highly scented and smells like a traditional bar of soap.

The shampoo bar doesn't lather like regular shampoo, but it covered my hair well. I think it would be beneficial if I use a mesh soap bag to help with the longevity of the shampoo bar. I love that it is environmental friendly and sustainable. It would last quite a while if stored properly. My only concern is that it is not very budget friendly. I suppose that would depend on how long the bar of soap lasts. This shampoo bar did cleanse my hair. I think it would be great paired with a conditioner bar for people with long or thick hair. I would like to try other scents.

reviews.text: This shampoo is imported from South Korea. The gel is actually clear and is not too thick - it reminds me more of shower gel than a shampoo. It has collagen which means it's meant to strengthen weak, brittle hair and is perhaps best for those with aging hair (in other words, better for older rather than younger people). Maybe because of the collagen, it has a slight medicinal scent but not off putting. It foams up pretty well and left my hair feeling really clean. I can't say it left my hair super soft as I still needed conditioner. Overall this is a pleasant if rather generic shampoo. Perhaps it strengthens your hair over time but since I just started using it I can't vouch for that.

reviews.title: Leaves hair nice but very strong perfumy fragrance.
reviews.text: The first thing I notice when I twisted up the pump to was a sweet odor that was not bad, but very  much like a perfume I smelled once. Then I pumped the shampoo out and started washing my hair.  Now, I am a 65 year old man.  I don't like strong odors and prefer lavender and citrus, but don't mind a mild odor of perfume.  This was so strong, I had to immediately rinse it out of my hair and use a citrus shampoo to eliminate the odor, yes, really, it was that strong. I looked at some other reviews, one of which says they detected no odor. So either something is wrong with quality control or I am too sensitive or the person who wrote that other review can't smell.  I am not that sensitive.  I am sure the other person can smell.  So I think it is quality control.  Therefore, I don't like it and yes, "nice" ingredients, but with that strong smell, I can't recommend it for anyone but someone who likes their perfume in their hair.

reviews.title: Amazing results after 1 use
reviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised by this product. I have natural virgin medium-dark brunette hair. In the summer months it gets very sun bleached and turns very brassy and a lot of red pops out. I have tried other products that didn’t do much to help but thought I would try one more and I am so happy I did. With 1 shampoo this product took probably 85-90% of the brassiness out of my hair. I started with a clarifying shampoo first then used this product and let it sit for 4 minutes then rinsed and followed up with my normal Verb conditioner. Not only was my hair softer then normal it smelled amazing and pretty much all of that brassiness was out of my hair. I will buy this product again and again and will recommend to everyone who struggles with brassy tones in their hair!

The MATRIX Total Results Dark Envy Color-Depositing Green Shampoo didn't alter or neutralize the brassy tones of my faded color and I was hard-pressed to see any difference. I tested it at the end of one of my braids (the on on the right that looks very red) and when comparing it to the other they looked exactly the same. It may work on lighter hair colors, mine is medium to dark auburn. As a shampoo, it is a bit drying. The one saving grace is that this shampoo did not stain my skin or fabric shower curtain liner. reviews.title: Has great qualities and see this only getting better..!!
reviews.text:
Wow! Such a different concept- this is smaller then I expected- (see photos included to compare sizing) I do suggest using with a slatted soap dish so it can stay dry.. For obvious reasons, if bar stays wet it will melt/dissolve and waste product.

Smell is amazing! Upon opening this has a florally fresh fragrance that smells clean and very pleasant. Scent does dissipate with use of blow dryer..

Created to provide hair better properties for health and results.. I find bar shampoo lathers a bit more then liquid but, easily rinses away without issue. Designed to apply by rubbing bar on hair itself- I struggle with this! I think it’s a sensory issue for me!? I find lathering in hand and placing onto hair still creates a solid application and fixed my angst!

What I love about this concept is the “going green effect..” Saving our planet from so much wasted plastic and packaging.. this concept alone deserves praise in that regard!! I also feel that being in a new space with this idea/concept.. we’ve only begun to see what it can do. This is a place where products have potential to just improve, grow and move into something grand.. for that I’m exited!!

Hair is left to feel soft and inviting- no issues with tangles or frizzies. Side note: I do pair this with pureology smoothing/humectant to help maintain control… as I do use blow dryer to my routine! It is a solid option and definitely a positive on helping the environment- hoping info can help make your decision.. stay safe everyone!

reviews.title: from a Curly Girl follower
reviews.text:
I've been following a modified version of Curly Girl for several years now. These products tick all the boxes in terms of being free of the bad stuff (silicones, etc ) and having the good stuff. The shampoo & conditioner left my hair very soft and shiny, but also more straight than normal, even when following my normal routine/ products. I'm not sure what's in there that my hair doesn't like.

The custard, though... not for me at all. Every time I've tried it (I gave it a chance!), a little or a lot, different application methods, no matter what: every time I get flaking. Literally clear flakes of product coming out of my hair all day long, forcing me to wash it two days in a row (which is drying to curly hair). It also did not hold or form curls for me at all.

So in conclusion, these are nice clean products that might work for someone else, but they didn't work for me.

reviews.text: I waited a little over a week to write a review bc I wasn’t sure at first if I loved this product or hated it. After the first few times I used it my verdict is... I love it! It is different than your typical conditioner that you use from a bottle that leaves your hair tangle free and smooth and silky straight out of the shower. But... this little bar of conditioner is pretty awesome. The reason I couldn’t figure out if I hated or loved it though was bc when I first rinse it out of my hair my hair is tangled and snarled and not soft at all. BUT..... after it dries my fingers run right through my hair like butter and it’s so soft. My scalp doesn’t itch, my ears and skin are not irritated. Which is great bc I am allergic to gluten which is in a lot of other bathroom products and my skin is sensitive. It’s a lightweight conditioner so my hair is not flat on my head, it has volume! Plus my scalp does not get super greasy after a day or two. I think this is a product that you grow to love and appreciate the more you use it. My only complaint is that I wish the scent were more feminine or fruity. It has a slightly musky/masculine scent. Also.... I just had to say, I was so impressed by the note that they put in the box. The owner of this company really cares about her customers and has a great heart. You can see it in the note and in the products they create. Thank you for a great product, I will be using this for a long time to come and letting my family and friends know about it!

reviews.title: Decent Conditioner That Delivered Some Good Results-(but not enough for me to continue using it)
reviews.text:
**FYI... REDKEN's Acidic Bonding Concentrate conditioner is part of a 3 step process. I did NOT do Step 1 and use the shampoo. I did steps 2 & 3 and used the conditioner and leave -in treatment ONLY**

Step 1-REDKEN's Acidic Bonding shampoo (I did NOT use this!)
Step 2-REDKEN's Acidic Bonding conditioner (used this)
Step 3-REDKEN's Acidic Bonding leave-in treatment (used this-and will write a separate review for it as well)

REDKEN's Acidic Bonding conditioner is meant to deliver intense conditioning while protecting hair color from fading, stop breakage/split ends and smooth hair. I like the consistency. Its a light and airy cream that is easy to apply to hair and doesn't take much to cover my shoulder length, thick hair. An amount slightly larger than a quarter covers my hair sufficiently. It rinses out easily as well. It does not weigh my hair down, nor does it cause my hair to look or feel oily/greasy. When my hair dries, my natural waves are nice and smooth and look good. It really does protect my hair color and doesn't cause it to fade. I've not experienced much hair breakage since using this conditioner but I do still have split ends. My hair is not de-tangled after using this conditioner though to be fair, it doesn't claim to de-tangle hair. I AM able to comb through the tangles nice and easy-no pulling or struggling to get them out. My is FAR from being hard after using this...it is soft but not super soft. There is a light citrus scent to this conditioner. I'm not a fan of citrus scent but this one is light and mild and doesn't last very long so its not an issue for me.

I don't know if I would experience better results had I used the shampoo as advised. This is a good conditioner that delivered some positive results for me. Unfortunately, it didn't deliver as many positive results as I would have liked. Due to this, and the cost of the conditioner, I have no plans to continue using this on a regular basis.

reviews.title: I’m… optimistic but cautious?
reviews.text:
Okay, so like many others, I read all the marketing words on this that make it sound like it’s a co-wash; hell, it even says “deep cleanse” on the front of the bottle. It isn’t, BUT I read through comments and noticed it did work for some as a co-wash, so I’m giving it a chance. My other co-wash I’ve used for years from a well-known brand is no longer being sold at Sally Beauty, it’s marked up x3-4 on Amazon, and their website doesn’t ship to Alaska for some reason… so I’m on the hunt for a new co-wash because having out-of-state family mail me my hair products is ridiculous. I tried this out as a co-wash today and as of right now, I’m cautiously optimistic. It doesn’t feel quite as clean and soft as my other brand, but it did definitely clean my hair; there’s no leftover residue readily apparent, although I am noticing a bit of frizz. I’m going to give my hair some time to adjust. Side note, the smell is beautiful!

About my hair: I have super-fine, thick, wavy hair, and it’s that infuriating curl type where if conditions are PERFECT (like, 3x in my life), all of my hair will naturally fall into these gorgeous large ringlets without any additional product—most of the time, though, I struggle with it being partially beachy-wavy and partially not-quite-flat-but-not-cute with a random ringlet here and there. This definitely wasn’t my best hair day since I just switched it up, but I’m going to try it out a bit more and monitor for any scalp or hair buildup. Fingers crossed this actually will work as a co-wash!

reviews.title: Makes my hair weighed down and feeling gunky
reviews.text:
I had received a sample size of this conditioner in a subscription box last year, and I liked it so much that I bought the full size almost immediately. Unfortunately, I was never able to replicate the results I had with that sample. This conditioner ends up weighing my hair down, makes my hair lank and stringy looking and makes it feel gunky and like its full of product. Honestly, it makes my hair look like I haven't washed it in a week. It becomes completely resistant to any kind of styling. I can barely even get a comb through it because it's so gunky feeling.
I have a lot of hair but it's become fine over the years. This conditioner does nothing positive for my hair. When I first used the sample my hair was extremely soft, shiny and bouncy. I don't really know what the deal is, but the full size product makes my hair completely the opposite.
I haven't used it more than 3 times, and each time I regret giving it another chance.

I used it last night because my hair was feeling kind of dry and I was getting my hair cut this morning and wanted my hair to not look and feel so dry. I was quickly reminded why it's been sitting in my cabinet unused. My stylist felt my hair this morning and just said "Throw that right in the trash". I'm following her advice so I don't make the mistake of trying to give it another shot.
It smells nice though, and it's rich and creamy, but it's hard to evenly distribute when working through the hair. I end up having to use a bit more than I normally would just so my ends don't go without. Perhaps that reason alone makes my hair look and feel like it does. So, if my choices are: not getting enough conditioner evenly distributed in my hair, or having my hair weighed down by product and feeling gross, I choose trash.
Definitely way more expensive than it should be, especially for the size and performance.
Definitely not a repurchase item, and it goes on my "regret purchasing" list.

reviews.text:
As a man I do buy high quality hair products - so I have opinions and my overall experience with this is very positive. For starters, the scent is pleasant and not overwhelming like many other products. I like the fact that when I took a shower and used it, it created like an aromatic experience, was soothing and relaxing. As for how my hair turned out, well... it was soft, not overly soft. I think after a few more washes and uses my hair will only get better in time.

As for the color of the product, admittedly I was slightly concerned. The color of the conditioner is an off white / beige color. I've got lighter brown hair so I've got no concerns over staining or coloring, but if say someone has bright blonde / white hair, I'd be more curious than anything what longterm usage may do for colorization, would it stain? Prob. not but only someone with very light hair can say.

I'm overall very happy with the product, I'll continue to use it and add it to my routine. If you're looking for something manly yet subtle, give this a shot.

Oh yea, I also like their minimalist logos / bottle design. It's nothing fancy which I greatly appreciate.

It was love at first shampoo for both of the shampoo types. They smell nice, but not strong, and left my normally dry hair feeling clean. The conditioner, oh my, smelled good and left my hair soft, shiny, and with a lot more lift and body than my usual shampoo. I liked it so well that I had my (85 years young) try the products on her very fine and thinning hair. Big difference for her because her hair is almost completely gray and changed completely after a series of chemo therapy treatments. I don't know if it was one of the shampoos or the conditioner or the combination of both, but you could see hints of her natural auburn color in with the darker gray hair. She said it was very easy to comb her hair out after washing it, and it was fuller and very soft. After only 2 uses of each shampoo, you could see the change-- it just looked very healthy!

reviews.title: No added volume

I put this Dove conditioner, along with the shampoo, in their bathroom for her to use on her beautiful long dark color-treated hair. I'm a retired hairstylist but have always loved Dove products over some of the pricier salon brands.
She says she loves the way the shampoo and conditioner smells, and that it feels really good as she washes and conditions her hair. She doesn't blow dry her hair, but it lays so much smoother and is much shinier.
The conditioner has Coconut Oil and other ingredients that moisturize and also close the cuticle, making it very soft, smooth, and silky. It almost looks like a different color now because it is so much healthier.

reviews.title: Adds body and texture to fine, limp hair when used occasionally
reviews.text: I love Pacifica Beauty Salty Waves Shampoo and Conditioner.  I first purchased it at Target and then found it here on Amazon for half the price.  I have fine, soft, long hair and lots of it.  I have difficulty finding products to "lift" my hair at the root and help it to look more full.  When my hair starts to get too soft or conditioned, I use this product for a couple of days and it really helps bring back the volume and bounce.  If I used it every day, it becomes harsh and over texturizes my hair leaving it dull and and rough.  So...know that this is a great once-a-week shampoo/conditioner but overuse may cause you to say goodbye to the product.

reviews.title: Lovely Banana Scent.  Leaves hair healthy!
reviews.text:
I quite love this conditioner, but I do not find it particularly enhances my wavy hair. However, it has a yummy sweet banana scent and (more importantly) conditions my hair very well. I don't find my hair any curlier/wavier after using it, but I do find it in particularly healthy condition. The results are soft, quite shiny, with good body, smooth and easy to style. It's a slightly thick conditioner, I find I use a generous amount to get it fully distributed.

I generally purchase salon conditioners (I rarely find a drug store one I truly like), and I have fine, thick-ish, wavy hair that tends to be dry (and has a very closed low porosity cuticle). My hair loves protein, and this has enough to content my hair.

With any product described as "Salty," I have the concern the results will be either dry or tangly, but no product in this line produces any sort of dryness or tangliness; they all leave hair well-controlled soft, and shiny. I'll be interested in retrying the balm and salt spray in the summer, as I think they may give more wave in warm humid weather and seem suited for air drying. But, in the meantime, I quite love the shampoo and conditioner.

reviews.text:
My husband and I both tried this conditioner, so you get a double review for this one, his is below. First things first, though. If you haven't gotten a spilled package in the mail, you've read angry reviews about them. This won't happen with this product - if they let us give a bonus star out every month, they would win it. I can't count the number of times I've gotten a half empty crusted up item because the bottle had no seal. Not only is this bottle sealed, but they have it in a baggie. LOVE! They are all about good first impressions...

As a female I was impressed that this wasn't just another heavy musky scent that many male-oriented products use. The scent is much more nuanced and sophisticated, not feminine but not something I have a problem smelling in my hair. I tend to use more fruity scented hair products. I would agree with his evaluation of the scent. We cheated and discussed it.

My first instinct upon application was that this wasn't, for lack of an easier word, slimy. I think sometimes conditioners do that to make you feel like your hair is moisturized and it might be a sort of lazy or easy way of expressing that to consumers. But I resisted the urge to use more and continued with my routine. This rinses out easily and I do seem to get less tangles than normal. I have waist length hair, so that's not something that goes unnoticed. My hair was pretty soft after use. I wouldn't say it's a huge difference from my usual conditioner after the brushing, but perhaps after more than just a few uses, and if I was also using the shampoo, I'd see a bigger difference. I think I'll leave this one for my husband but I do like it! He seems to have a better effect from using it. We both have long hair, mine is very thin though, his is very thick. That could be the difference, or maybe it really is just made for guys lol

Now for his perspective:

I would say the 8oz Volumizing Men's Conditioner by PUUR is better than anything I've bought at big-box stores.

I was skeptical right after applying the conditioner because it rinsed away pretty easily. That can be a bad sign for us long-haired folks. But I could tell after towel drying my hair that this conditioner is on a different level. My hair was much softer after just one use. After a few, I could tell a big difference. Also my brush went right through my hair with no tangles! What a relief.

My hair after the shower smells of vanilla, with just a hint of coconut and maybe a touch of leather?

This is well worth the price, I'll definitely keep using it and plan to get the 16oz next time.

reviews.title: Overpriced, Overhyped, Underwhelming, Smelled Bad
reviews.text:
I got this along with the shampoo, and while that was disappointing. This was even more so.

This is around $30 and worth it? No. I’m sorry, but for that much money, the product has to meet my requirements:

🧴Easy to Use (shape of container and dispensing)
👃🏻Smells Good
💯✅Delivers Good Results

And, this? Kind of on the gross side.

Like the matching shampoo, the bottle is decently shaped – thin and tall. Easy to grip and hold for most people.

That’s the ONLY good thing.

Like the shampoo, dispensing the product? Almost a full-blown work out. This is NOT EASY TO USE by any means. Anyone with weak hands, leave the building for this one.

While the shampoo had a honey-like consistency, this was almost like a thin type of paste. Not easy to squeeze through the hole. Like the shampoo, I opted for taking the cap off, shaking the product down and GLOPPING it in my hand. Not very cost effective.

As with most conditioners, I needed a bit more than recommended.

Scent? It has the nostalgic “salon” smell. Depending on your preference that is either good or bad. This had a decent smell in the bottle. On my twice washed hair? Absolutely disgusting 🤢 I couldn’t rinse it out fast enough. It might’ve been the alcohol, but I’ve NEVER had a condition smell that awful on my hair after I’ve shampooed it TWICE.

Good results? That’s a no go here too 😔 I’ve had much better results from a $5 bottle of Garnier. It is MUCH easier to use and smells FAR better.

For me, this is more hype than function. And, at the price – it’s definitely not winning me over.

reviews.text:
What a difference this conditioner makes in my hair. The very first time I tried L'Oreal Paris' Ever Pure Purple Conditioner, I could see a noticeable reduction to the brassiness in my blond hair. It did take a few uses to get all of my hair the same, even tone and now its exactly as it should be. It doesn't just neutralize the brassiness; in addition, it softens, hydrates and nourishes hair. I never have tangles after using it either. It has a nice scent to it though it doesn't last long at all. By the time my hair dries (I air dry), I can no longer smell the scent. Its easy to work into as well as rinse from hair.

I have very dry, sensitive skin and have no negative reactions using this conditioner. It does contain purple dye but I also have no issues with the dye coloring my hair/skin purple. I don't need to use much conditioner at all to sufficiently cover my shoulder length hair and with the bottle being 33oz, this will last me quite some time!

Its wonderful to have that uneven brassy blond out of my hair. I use this conditioner once a week and am thrilled with with it. For the amazing and fast results it delivers and the huge size bottle, I find the price more than reasonable and definitely recommend it for those with color treated, blonde, bleached, silver and brown w/highlights hair.

This is a great purple conditioner by L'Oreal. It comes in a generous bottle. The conditioner has a fantastic fragrance that I really like. It has a deep purple color that will help counter the brassiness in blonde, bleached, silver or brown highlighted hair.

I usually let it sit in my hair for about 5 minutes but longer works as well and the time really depends on how much of an effect you need since you are basically depositing purple color in your hair. It rinses out with easy and I never had any purple color on my hands, body or anywhere in the shower. My hair was easy to brush through and once it was dry it was nice and soft. All in all this is a great conditioner that is also not very expensive.
