reviews.title: Another Awesome Nature Nut Product
reviews.text:
I just knew I would love Nature Nut's Deep Conditioning Hair mask! I'm already a fan of their leave in conditioner and face cream, so I wasn't surprised when the mask delivered excellent results as well.

I could have gotten away with using 2/3 of a pack to sufficiently cover my thick, shoulder length hair but I went ahead and used an entire pack. Its easy to work into hair and just as easy to rinse out. Though the instructions say to allow it to sit on hair 2-3 minutes, I left it on for 5. It detangled my hair beautifully. I didn't have even one tangle when I combed it. When my hair dried (i air dry), my natural waves and curls were soft, smooth and shiny. My hair doesn't shine on its own so its always a good thing when a product allows it to! The day after I used the mask I spent a good deal of time outside in the hot sun planting tomato plants and flowers and had worked up a sweat. My hair frizzes when I get sweaty but it didn't following the use of this mask.

There is a scent to this that I very much like though it didn't last very long.

This is an exceptional mask. It revived my hair while delivering shine, softness and smoothness. My normally dry hair became moisturized and hydrated. The instructions say to use it 1-3 times per week and I plan on doing just that. I've already purchased a 2nd box! I also gave my mom a packet too to try ; I have a hunch she'll soon place an order of her own as well! lol. The price is more than reasonable. This mask delivers salon -quality results to my hair and I absolutely recommend it. Perfect for all hair types!

reviews.title: Virtually no suds in my HE washer, soft clothes & a bargain!
reviews.text: The editor of a major women's magazine recently touted the powder version of this product; mostly she liked being able to order online and have it delivered to her house. Because of sensitive skin, I have used liquid detergents for years, even making my own low-suds recipe for awhile but gave that up when I discovered a major eco-friendly brand that was low-sudsing and didn't irritate my skin. After reading about this product, I went to the Charlie's Soap website and tracked the 32-oz liquid container (for $10) to a local store. It was a bit pricey for the size, but since it is just my husband and me (three adult sons are in and out very irregularly), I decided to give it a try. The first thing I liked about the bottle was the built-in measurer with markings in both ounce and milliliter. Squeeze the bottle and the soap goes up the tube on the side of the bottle into the measurer and you pour it directly into your washer's soap dispenser, then the cap screws back on. No separate, messy lid or spillage to deal with. There is a second cap to unscrew, with a regular large opening, because this handy container is refillable from the gallon jug. The packaging says to run a couple loads with rags to clean the old detergent out of the washer; I didn't do that so my first load was bit sudsy, so I ran the load several times to get out any old suds. I couldn't believe how naturally soft my clothes were (I haven't used fabric softener in years since we have softened water). I also like that there is no added fragrance, and the soap doesn't have any particular natural fragrance. The ingredients listed are washing soda, coconut oil and other natural cleaners. Also, my HE washer is very clean now and doesn't have that stale, mildewed smell (I always leave the door open when not in use). Charlie's Soap is made for HE washers, and the directions say to use no more than one ounce per load, even a large load. I do that, and even with softened water the soap generates practically no suds. If there are suds, it's because I'm washing clothes or other items that have old detergent in them. I cannot say enough good things about Charlie's Soap, and considering that I paid $10 for the 32-oz container, this four-gallon multipack is quite a bargain. I also signed up for the six-month autosubscribe (the maximum time, which I will adjust if necessary) so there was another small discount for that. Yes, it does seem a bit weird to order laundry soap online, but considering the savings and that it is delivered to my door (in a box that my cats love), I got over the weirdness pretty quickly.

reviews.title: Effective, not-toxic staple!
reviews.text: I have been using Molly's Suds for 5 years now and it is on my Subscribe & Save list.  I experimented with a few different non-toxic laundry detergents after I had my first child and ended up sticking with this one.  I also buy the other laundry products Molly's offers, which I enjoy, but this one is my staple.  It leaves no scent.  I know some reviewers say they smell a slight fresh scent, but I really don't smell anything.  My clothes simply smell clean.  I have a front loader HE washing machine, but I have also used this in a top loader and have been equally happy.  I do more laundry than most typical families and have a lot of high end, expensive children's clothing that I wash at home on a cold wash/hang dry.  I wash mostly in cold but also use Molly's Suds for the super hot sanitize options for towels and regular hot washes for sheets and other regular clothes.  This soap works equally well in all washes.  I have played around with how much, and have found that one scoop directly in the empty drum and one scoop in the soap dispenser works best.  I also use vinegar in my bleach and softener dispensers.  When I have medium to large loads, I also do a presoak as I find this helps get everything thoroughly saturated.  I have fragrance sensitivities and Molly's Suds has never caused me any discomfort.  My son has eczema and I have never noticed any irritation.  A note that I do not use this product with any of my woolens (I use Soak, which I have also reviewed).  My one negative is that I do not love their packaging.  I find the bag does not zip closed after opening because the powder gets into the zip track.  I have also noticed that I receive this product often with powder all over the box and any other items in the box even though I do not see any holes or damage to the product's packaging.  I don't think this is a huge deal--I simply empty the bag into a large glass pantry type container, which  sits on my countertop and is much prettier anyway.  Highly recommend this product, especially for anyone who does not like strong fragrance or has small children.

reviews.title: Such an easy way to be earth friendly!
reviews.text:
In a nutshell:

*Dissolves well in my top loader with cold water
*Clothes come out perfectly clean and have just a hint of scent
*My very sensitive skin has not been irritated
*Actually saves me money compared to old traditional detergent

The long version:

I am so impressed with this product, I had been slightly worried when I ordered it because of bad experiences in the past with eco friendly detergents, but I'm so glad I took the chance.

I've been using a detergent that rhymes with 'ride' for a long time but I've been looking for small ways I can make my home and family more ecologically friendly like switching to bar soaps and using my clothesline whenever possible. These little soap strips really cut down on the weight that is shipped and I love that their packaging isn't plastic, not to mention the detergent ingredients are much better for the environment than what I have been using.
I know some people have said that the strips didn't dissolve in the wash for them or just didn't clean their clothes, but they've worked great for me in my top loading washer in cold water.
I haven't had any issues with clothes still being dirty after they've been washed, clothes from my 3 kids who love crafts and playing outside, mine and my husband's workout clothes, etc all come out clean and smelling nice.
I also have ridiculously sensitive skin, with the pandemic I can tell when a store has been cleaning because my skin instantly breaks out in a painful rash, this detergent hasn't caused any issues with my skin, which is huge.
The other thing that has made me so happy is the price. With my former detergent I almost always had to use two pods to get clean clothes which meant detergent for 1 load cost about 61 cents. One strip of this detergent gets all but the muddiest loads clean, which means a load costs about 50 cents. How awesome is it that the eco friendly option is less expensive?

reviews.title: Works OK, not much better than other free and clear products
reviews.text:
The microfiber towel is brand new and was put in the wash with towel kleen. Notice the discoloration.

I purchased some towel kleen from Autogeek for significantly less than the $30 Amazon is currently offering (closer to $20 with free shipping). I wanted to try it out on my microfiber car detailing towels.

Normally I use Purex free and clear, which is under $10 for about 1.5 gallons from Walmart or other big box stores. You don't want your detergent to have dyes, fragrances, bleach, or fabric softeners added in, otherwise you'll ruin your microfiber towels.

The towel kleen solution comes in a jug without a pour spout. Not a huge issue, but it would help transfer liquid into the cup or directly into the washing machine. It is recommended to use about 2 oz of liquid per load. This soap creates A LOT of bubbles and my load size is only about 10-15 mid sized towels max. After the first few loads I decided to only use 1 oz, as 2 caused the water to be too sudsy in my opinion with so few towels.

This product definitely kept my microfiber towels slightly fluffier than the purex I was previously using. Not a ton, but enough to where you can feel the slight difference. Is it worth 2-3x the price for the added softness? Probably not.

My major complaint against this product is that it has caused staining on several of my towels. My washing maching is an HE front loader, so liquid is added to a dispenser at the top that later drips down into the basket. While folding some of my towels, I've noticed streaks of detergent in the towels. I used the extra rinse option to increase the amount of time the towels are in the water, but even that didn't prevent streaks. It might just be discoloration, but it makes clean towels look dirty/unsafe to use on car paint.

At over 2x the price and leaving streaks with the only added benefit being a little bit more fluffiness, I can't recommend this product.

reviews.title: Gets a Large Load of Laundry Clean and fresh Smelling
reviews.text:
Doing laundry is an ongoing, never- ending household necessity so anything that can make the process faster and/or more convenient is a welcome relief. Laundry detergent pods are great for this reason and one that I can add to my list of quality options is Gain Ultra Flings Liquid Laundry Detergent Pacs Designed for Large Loads, Original Scent.

Gain Ultra Flings are so named because they are intended for large loads of laundry and carry a strong scent. Yes, these pods are not intended for small loads- there is excessive detergent and scent for only a small or medium wash load. These are meant for an extra large load and they have no problem at all getting your laundry clean and fresh smelling. The added Oxi boost and Fabreeze makes a difference, too.

Speaking of the scent, this is something to keep in mind if you decide to use Gain Ultra Flings. The original Gain scent is on full display here and while most people like this famous aroma, it can be a bit much and with these pods, it does linger in your clothing for a while. This could be an issue for those with allergies and it could make these pods unsuitable for those with extremely sensitive skin.

I find that Gain Ultra Flings do take a little longer to dissolve, but not too much longer so this shouldn’t be an issue. The price is somewhat steep, too, but this is one laundry detergent that cleans and freshens as promised. If you love the scent of original Gain and you love convenience, Gain Ultra Flings Detergent Pacs are an excellent addition to your laundry routine.

reviews.title: Mostly works
reviews.text:
I have a lot of activewear (Nike, Under Armour, etc) that has been downgraded to farm/outdoor work clothing because it stinks. I do laundry every day so it wasn’t like I was letting my sweaty clothing sit around, some of those materials just pick up gunk and funk and don’t let go of it.

I tried the Hex Performance Laundry Detergent on a load of those clothes. In addition to sweat buildup, I also had dirt, oil, and maybe some grease on them.

I don’t particularly like the thin consistency of the Hex detergent. It really does pour like water, so I have to be careful not to accidentally pour too much into the washer.

I also don’t like the Lavender Fields scent -- I noticed the overwhelming scent of lavender the second I took my clothes out of the washer. It’s a strong, artificial scent that does not fade.

But I didn’t smell any of that yucky leftover sweaty stink on my clothing! So at first I thought the Hex detergent worked as promised and got rid of the funky odors. And oh, my clothes were clean of all the other yucky things, too.

However… I noticed that the label says, “It creates a shield against stains, stink, and static.” Today I wore one of the shirts washed with Hex. I was basically soaked in sweat by the time I was finished and my shirt stunk again. There was no stink shield.

Right off we needed three packs for a load. That’s all right, we knew that due to size and level of “soil” (dirty socks). Sadly, our water isn’t the best. We also needed another round of 2 packs. So, five (5) total for one load.

Initially, I thought the dress might have had some odd pigment that came from a broken down fiber since the dress was over 50 years old. Then I washed my sweater a couple of weeks later and big green-blue blotches formed all over it. I used a tiny amount of soap and gently swished it around. reviews.title: No scent left behind. Cleaned my dish towels fine.
reviews.text:
These CLEACE Laundry Detergent Soap Pods in Original Scent are just okay laundry detergent pods. One pod is only meant to do a small load of laundry, consisting of eight to 12 pieces only. Because the only small loads of laundry I do are usually my dish towels, I used one pod for washing them.
The writing on the back that tells you how to use these is so small that I had to put magnifier glasses over my regular glasses just to read it. That is way too small! It says that it is best to soak the pod before washing, so I let it soak in the water with the towels for about 30 minutes to dissolve, then started the wash. That is a little too much of a hassle for me.
The towels seemed to come out clean, and there was no residue left on them. These laundry pods are very lightly scented, and they don't leave any remaining scent behind after drying. My towels smelled clean, but I can't say how well dirty sweaty gym or work clothes might smell after washing them. I think you would need to use three pods to do a large load of clothes, which could get a bit expensive.
These laundry detergent pods are just okay, for me. They are not made of organic, or any other special ingredients. They seem to be made of just chemicals, like the myriad of laundry detergent pods out there. I'm not fond of using so many to do a large load of laundry, letting them soak, and I'm one that likes my laundry to smell good after washing it.
The laundry pods come in a nice plastic box, the pods are very small, and the whole lot takes up little space. If you are just looking to try out a new laundry pod, I would recommend giving them a try.

reviews.title: Cleans well
reviews.text: I used these pods on some blankets my cat has been using after recovering from a surgery. They are really easy to use. I used two for a large load. I definitely think they did a great job at getting the laundry clean. There were some tough stains they did not remove. I’m pretty sensitive to scents and I didn’t love the smell they left behind. It was kind of a “sterile” smell, but I will definitely use these up. They work pretty well!

reviews.title: Cleans smaller loads of laundry
reviews.text:
So these are really small pods…especially compared to other laundry pods. I was actually surprised when I opened them at the small size. Per the instructions, the laundry capacity per pod is 8-12 pieces of clothing. Disappointing as my loads of laundry are always much larger than that. I tried it on a smaller load consisting of kitchen towels and dishrags. The pod itself had a nice clean scent and seemed to dissolve well without any residue left on the laundry. Post wash I noticed no scent at all. This could be a plus for people sensitive to smells.

Other things worth mentioning… The container that holds the pods is great and really saves on space. Per the directions…for the pod to be more effective, you should soak the pods for a period of time pre-wash. I just don’t have time for that. I like to toss it in and go.

Since you only get 50 pods in the container and have to increase a pod every 8-12 items, I just don’t think that this product is very cost effective at the current price point

reviews.title: Easy to use pods for small loads
reviews.text:
I have used these a couple times now and during those times, I would either add an extra pod or use one pod less.
The result seems to be the same where I don't really notice a difference. There is no scent, but my cloths do smell cleaner. There is no smell of body odor left behind, but what bothers me is the fact that I can't tell if adding more or less pods to the laundry makes a difference.
Additionally, when washing I don't really see any bubbles that would form when compared to using regular detergent.

Overall, I think the pods does the job, but with the price tag, I would just stick with the go to laundry pod brands. I just don't feel convince that the amount of detergent packed in each pod is enough to clean a regular size load of laundry. Each pod is about half the size of a regular pod.

reviews.title: Stuff smells like magic
reviews.text: I've used this brands Cotton Fresh, Royal Linen, and the one they have for pets and I love all of them. And so does my family. My son is doing a load of laundry right now and it smells so damn good in the laundry room. It smells like a really expensive, unoffensive Cologne. Very clean and very addicting scent. I honestly don't think a Cologne would be necessary with this detergent. I've seen women say they use it for themselves. It's a tad too muscular for me but I can see why women would like it. It's a delicious scent. In fact, if this scent was an actual Cologne I would buy it for my son, husband, and father for a gift. That is how good Mambo Man smells. My son says he has never smelled an actual Cologne that smells as good as this detergent. I think a lot of men would really like this detergent. reviews.title: Pleased
reviews.text:
We initially ordered the trial-variety pack. I highly recommend doing this in spite of the costs. The scent I would have 'guessed' I liked wasn’t what we gravitated to at all.

We like several of the scents, but hands down our favorites were Mambo Man and Royal Linen. Mambo would be considered more masculine (we're both women), but once washed it was hard to top, especially on our linens and bleached clothes.

We ordered the larger size of Mambo Man to really give it a hard-run on our laundry.

Pros:
1.) Cleans well! We work in healthcare and having clean scrubs is a must.

2.) Environmentally friendly. I wanted to know a bit more about ‘how’ they are environmentally conscious. That’s not apparent other than mention of the use of bioenzymes — but I believe there are patens for their formulations/process, so that may be why there isn’t more disclosure. The science skeptic in me would like to know more about their process.

3.) The scent does linger pleasantly. I've been using another brand of detergent (Tyler High Maintenance and Kathina) which are some of my favorite scents, but without being environmentally conscious. Having products that are good for our bodies and earth matter greatly to me. So we’ll being using Hiketron here forward.

4.) After purchase and a review I heard from the company. I found this impressive and interesting. Consistent, honest customer service is uncommon, and a challenging thing to offer your buyers, especially in the face of growth. I hope they continue to make this a focal point as its one the best (and hardest) way to grow a solid base of loyalty.

Cons:

1.) If I could have a concern or con it would be cost. I think explaining to buyers why the cost is justifiable would be helpful. We can afford more expensive detergents, but the average buyer cannot. I've shared my enthusiasm for the product line with several friends and family. Several of whom couldn't justify the expense. It's concentrated and so I believe you get more bang-for-your-buck, but I had a hard time convincing family to drop the cash. Give us a rationale for why its necessary to pay more.

The instructions for this is to full the cap (1/3 cup ) of these crystals, and put them in the bottom of the washer.

These Arm & Hammer disolved, but did not take the smell out at all from my sons chef clothes that I was hoping for.
I also use a special detergent that works better for the scent then this does, as I could smell that one.
My son is a head chef for a up-scale dinner steak restaurant. I mention this, as the food is not heavy with different seasonings.

That said, for regular washing it seems to work well, but not what I was hoping for chef clothes.

reviews.title: I did not see any improvement with how fresh my laundry smelled
reviews.text:
These odor blasters are very fragrant and smell nice before going into the washer. I do not use anything like this normally and usually just use Tide detergent. When the clothes were done, they did not smell any fresher than normal. It was if I threw nothing in the laundry. Now my clothes are not particularly odoriferous, so perhaps that is the issue. I just would not buy this for me based on the results I am seeing. I tried Downy Unstoppables over six months ago and did notice a temporary freshness from those "in-wash scent beads" but still nothing that lasted that would make me want to buy that either.

reviews.title: Wonderful scent!
reviews.text: A client of my alterations shop brought me a sweatshirt to repair that she had washed with this product. It smelled so heavenly, that I begged to know what detergent she had used. She gave me a sample and from then on my family was hooked! When the price recently went way up, we decided to try the Downy Scent boosters, but we were very meh! about that product's scent and lasting power. I also like that this is a detergent too, not just a pretty smell. I use my Tide Pods with this as an add-on especially for a large load. It is a bit pricey but if my husband loves it, it's well worth it. He's actually the one who orders it!

reviews.title: Works Well
reviews.text:
I was solicited by the owner of the company to write a review of this product which I am glad to do. I have sensitive skin, and if not using dye free detergent I develop uncomfortable itching. I work out 6 times a week and do one laundry a week, with all clothing, towels that need to be washed and have been using WIN for 4 (weeks) loads so far. Everything appears clean, free of odor; perhaps the cotton items feel softer than before.
So, as of now, WIN has met all my expectations.

The only problem I have found is with the cap. The detergent comes with a screw on cap, covered with a green measuring cap, as shown in the pic. Consequently, after adding WIN to the machine, the Green cap leaks over the container (most measuring caps screw on) if placed back on. This is a minor problem, corrected by rinsing the cap before storing the container or not placing the cap on the container

reviews.title: Does the trick, but man is it expensive!
reviews.text:
I have to wear body armor every day for work. Under that armor, I wear compression-type shirts to wick the moisture away from my body. Needless to say, in the summertime those undershirts get nasty. Regular detergent wasn't getting the job done so I started trying the different specialty brands out there. This is one of the few brands that actually gets the job done. That being said, I have to use close to twice the recommended amount per load, so it goes quickly. The bottle is VERY small to begin with, so I run out quickly. If the price point was comparable to regular detergent this would be getting 5 stars. If it was just a little more expensive it would be getting 4 stars, but since it's soooo much more expensive (per fl oz), I had to knock it 2 stars.

Bottom line: If you don't mind the cost, this WILL keep your compression gear smelling fresh regardless of how it smelled going into the washer...

reviews.title: Good for biological stains, no so good for inorganic stains
reviews.text:
I bought this detergent to try with the Dirty Labs booster. I have an aging septic system and live rurally so I can't use "normal" laundry detergents.

I have the unscented one since my family has sensitive skin and we've found that some members of my family have had skin rashes since switching.

The detergent itself works well with the booster on biological stains. Dish towels, reusable cleaning cloths, pet bedding have all been great. It has also worked great on my gym clothes.

It definitely takes some retraining of your brain that such a teeny tiny dose cleans! If you look on the back of other eco friendly detergents water is the first ingredient so you are paying for more water! This is a concentrated product but even so it is a low number of washes per container.

We wash big loads to make better use of the well water on our property and be more economical with energy use. Most of our clothes are line dried unless it's winter then we tumble dry.

I love the silicone measuring cup, after pouring the detergent into the machine, I toss the measuring cup in the washer too so I get all the dose into the wash. It is a bit hard to see the dosing lines on the cup of you have low lighting in your laundry room.

I do love that the container is small and easily recycled (it's aluminium), but I'm not sure how to recycle the silicone measuring cup.

It is more expensive for a small number of laundry loads and the detergent itself has not been able to clean inorganic stains like mud/dirt, the detergent hasn't worked for soot or mineral based grease stains like sunscreen in my HE machine without extensive pre-treating with laundry soap hence 3 out of 5 stars.

Would I buy it again? Possibly. I'm trying different brands to see if my family can find one that cleans and doesn't cause rash/irritation. If this came in a bigger size I would be tempted to make the switch.

reviews.title: I love the idea of these lightweight laundry sheets. Also they’re the least expensive on Amazon.
reviews.text:
I love the idea of these lightweight laundry sheets because they take up less space, don’t put another plastic bottle in recycling bins or landfills, and are economical.

I did a medium load with one laundry sheet. While my clothes came out clean, there was no fragrance to them. Some people may welcome this as they’re sensitive to scents, I like a little fragrance.

The next load, I tried two laundry sheets in the same amount of laundry, just to see if it make a difference.
My clothes smelled clean enough, but I missed a slightly stronger detectable fresh scent. Nothing extreme or heavy, just a little more. There were no residual odors with two sheets.

As for stains, the only thing is to pretreat with a little liquid shampoo, just in case you didn’t know that trick.

This is probably one of the best practical inventions I have seen in a long time. Why don’t all laundry detergent companies use this technology? It would certainly help the landfills.

reviews.title: Works well in my HE washing machine
reviews.text:
I used these laundry sheets in my HE washing machine in warm water for 2 loads of laundry: one load of heavy towels (no stains) and a load of clothes and a towel heavily stained with dirt. Both loads came out clean.

I’m not a fan of scented laundry detergent (I always buy unscented detergents), so I was a little concerned about the “fresh linen scent”. However, the scent of the sheet itself is very mild and I didn’t notice that my clothes had a scent after using these sheets. Note that the “fresh linen scent” isn’t mentioned anywhere on the box or in the instructions (just “fragrance factors” mentioned in the list of ingredients.)

The localization of the instructions into English isn’t very good (“The dry or damp product doesn’t influence the washing effect in the use process.”), but overall, it’s pretty easy to understand how to use these laundry sheets: depending on how heavily stained (and how heavy) the clothing is, use one, two, or three laundry sheets.

Price-wise, these sheets are a good deal (current price is $14.99) for 120 sheets and 4 tablets to clean your washing machine.

I received these laundry sheets in August 2021 and they had an expiration date of April 11, 2024. These laundry sheets are made in China.

reviews.title: The Laundry Detergent that Does it All
reviews.text:
Do you fret over laundry detergent? I don’t, at least not usually. I avoid the brands I feel are overpriced and I have been known to sample a bargain brand or two, just to test them and see how well they work. But one of the better brand names that isn’t overpriced is All Laundry Detergent and its Stainlifter version easily passes the tests of quality.

I prefer liquid detergent and pods for my laundry needs because I don’t like the messiness of powders. This detergent is liquid and produces only a moderate amount of suds. Some liquids suds up a little too much, often to the point where you need a second rinse to remove all of the soap. All Stainlifter keeps the suds under control and with only about 1.5 ounces needed for each load, the relatively small bottle will get you through about 33 loads of dirty laundry provided you’re careful about how much you use. It’s easy to use too much because the markings on the inside of the cap are hard to see. My recommendation is to take the empty cap and pour 1.5 ounces of water inside it. This way, you will get a rough idea exactly where 1.5 ounces is when you use the detergent.

Cleaning of course is the real clincher for any laundry detergent and All Stainlifter earns good marks as a cleaning agent. It powers away stains and leaves clothing smelling good but not too perfumey. My clothing doesn’t usually get very stained except when I’m doing lawn work. This liquid detergent has no problem handling the stains.

All detergents have been around for a long time and while All may not be as well known as other brand names, it’s still a very good detergent. All Stainlifter gets the job done and for a competitive price. It earns my seal of approval and rates with the best of them.

reviews.title: Life ruining rash
reviews.text: Let me preface with this: I am 51 years old and have never had an allergic reaction to anything in my life.  Because of that, when I started to have symptoms, I did not direct our family doctor towards possible skin allergies, because I had never had them before, and especially never thought to connect a "hypo allergenic" laundry soap to the worst physical crisis I have ever had to endure.  What started as a small rash (a few itchy bumps) on my upper right shoulder, in August, progressed slowly until it turned into full body hives, welts and scabs by November.  Over the course of those 4 months, as more and more of my personal clothing and household items were washed in Costco's ultra clean hypo allergenic laundry soap, my condition continued to get worse, but I had no idea why it was happening.  By November, my existence had been whittled down to three categories: scratching, trying not to scratch or crying.  It may sound over the top, but when I tell you this detergent ruined my life I am not exaggerating.  I was unable to focus on anything for longer than a few minutes at a time due to the constant prickly sensation and the urge to itch.  I was unable to sleep.  I quit working out.  I could not physically relax my mind or my body for any length of time, due to the constant urge to itch, or in trying to fight the itch.  It was nothing short of mental and physical torture.  It finally dawned on me to have a second look at my laundry soap.  It was then that I realized that I had switched to the Costco brand likely around the time the shoulder rash had started.  I was floored.  A hypoallergenic laundry soap could be the cause of this life ruining full body rash??  I stopped using it THAT DAY and started rewashing everything in a vinegar - baking soda cycle, twice per load (4 washes total per load), just to be sure.  The rewashing alone took a week.  It is now three weeks later, and although I am 75% improved, I am still not out of the woods.  I’m still taking Zyrtec and a prescription medicine, but taking much less than I was.  I’m sure there will be residue in my clothing/bedding for several more washes, before it’s completely cleared out.  It feels like a miracle, but I have my life back.  For a while there, I didn't know if my life would ever be normal again…all because of a laundry detergent that’s supposed to be made for sensitive skin.

reviews.title: Great problem solver not daily user…
reviews.text:
Ordered Forever New “Stretch active” detergent for my varsity collegiate athlete and let’s just say.. She can stink!! The fact is, sport uniforms.. especially her workout clothes from 2 a day practices (washed daily!) can hold onto nasty smells- especially the stretchable underlayer.. Spanks, Sport bras, Socks, Panties… Not a good thing!! Truth is.. my girl is a beast on the field but she likes to embrace her soft, clean, feminine side when she takes of her cleats..

Doing wash daily I had a vigorous routine.. soap pod, scent booster, softener and dryer sheet! Im a wizard at removing stains + brightening colors but even my pricey concoction.. was “covering up and masking” issues while irritating her skin!!

Stretch Active (baby powder scent) has stepped up in the washing arena and I’ve seen some differences. Using only detergent and dryer sheet.. skin feels better and after x3-4 cycles of Stretch- smell has all but dissipated. The biggest offenders: sport bras, socks, panties- I had to do a handwash soak in the sink.. after x3 round- it seems clothing has let go of unfavorable smell! *I’ve found using in a hand wash setting, detergent is far more effective at getting smells to vacate. Im just not sure how realistic that is as a daily solution.. Especially if wanting to use on towels that seem to hold onto that old water smell?

Mine didn’t include directions/proportion amount- as of now, I’m using x1 full scoop included inside (like baby formula!) With small/med. load- added directly to h2o flow into drum. I see the smaller 16oz jar will go fast! So, best to be intentional with the use of Stretch or it will prove costly!

I suggest the product for on hand solution when items hold onto smells you don’t want! It’s a resource/rescue of sorts for me. Bc of price I plan to use in this capacity.. with a family of 6 and loads of daily laundry- a jar would only last a week! Hoping info can help make your decision.. stay safe everyone.

reviews.title: Love the detergent! Hate the packaging. Both tabs already broke.
reviews.text:
I'm really loving these Persil Laundry Detergent Discs with Active Scent Boost. They really get my clothes clean. There is no residue, stiff feeling, or residual odor left behind after washing my dark clothes, which is what I tried this with first, like I had with my other detergent. I guess I thought it was pretty normal, until after washing a medium load with one of these. They just feel different, and they smell so good and clean. I'm a sucker for great smelling laundry, and this detergent leaves your clothes smelling wonderful! I like this better than any detergent I've tried. It really does get your clothes clean and the discs are so easy.
A big thing I'm not fond of is the packaging. I know it needs to be childproof, but does it really need to be adult proof, too? I have three different types in these discs, and at least one of the little tabs snapped on each package the first time trying to open them. On one package, both snapped off. I have strength issues, but they just don't open as easily as it shows. I'm going to have to put them into something else, which defeats the purpose of packaging altogether. It seems like it could have been designed much better.
And another thing... Why only 59 pods? Why not an even 60? Most will not use three pods each time, and it is such an odd number to put in/on a package. I don't get why you didn't just add one more... But, that's just me being knit picky.
Besides the horrible adult proof packaging, I really love these Persil Detergent Discs. I would likely repurchase the liquid version, unless they make better packaging, but I definitely recommend it!

reviews.title: They really work well, fresh long lasting light aroma, not perfumy
reviews.text:
Works well, smells good. No problems!

Admittedly I was skeptical at first. I have used laundry sheets before, but I was unsure of these given how small they are. See, there are 16 sheets, but each sheet has a perforation making it 2 portions per sheet, for a total of "32". The full (2 portions) sheet size is what I am used to from my other sheets. A third portion (so, 1.5) sheets are suggested to be used on extra large loads, like towels and bedding. Making it a bit less than 32 loads. So keep that in mind when considering this.

I proceeded with using one full sheet per large load, no matter what it was. I have done 2 full loads of laundry so far. First load was heavily soiled rags (I clean homes for a living) in hot water, and the second load was normal soiled clothing, in cold water. I had both filling as maximum loads. I used one full sheet for each (which is two rectangles). I considered a third portion as per instructions on the extra dirty towels/rags, but I was curious how well 2 portions would do for it.

Both loads turned out clean and fresh smelling. Very light scent, but it simply smells clean. I think I will go ahead and use the 3rd portion next time I do a full load of extra dirty cleaning rags, but even with the 2 they came out well.

The fresh aroma continued through the drying cycle, and well after folding and putting away. Yet not perfumed smelling. Just a fresh, clean smell. Performed better than expected. I will likely continue with my huge bottles of liquid detergent (love my Tide, and Era), but I do pick up a box/packet of laundry sheets to use when I feel like it, and want something extra easy. I really do love how little space it takes up in my laundry area.

I used this in a top loading washer. Sheet appears to have dissolved completely.

5 stars because it works well, has pleasant light fresh scent.

reviews.title: day after this arrived I had several loads of cat pee laundry to do. WORKS
reviews.text:
Well, I can say I have used it what it is intended for. Excellent timing too. I had to do several loads of laundry just after receiving this because a slew of bedding was peed on. I have a home office that has a couple of twin beds set up in an "L" shape to create a large sitting/lounging space for my big labs and (and formerly elderly cats, RIP). Recently we adopted two young adult cats. This room became their home base as we work through transitions. Its not going exactly well, and recently one or both began peeing on the beds. No medical issues, so we're looking at behavioral and making adjustments. So forward to me spending the day (yesterday) stripping beds, washing everything (I have lots of pillows on there too as back rests), etc.. wiping down floors and everywhere else with a bio cleaner. I immediately put this laundry detergent to the test.

It doesnt have a strong fragrance. Not much in comparison to regular detergents. I added detergent initially by using the cup that it came with, but it is ridiculously hard to tell where the indicators are. So I just guessed on all the other loads. I think I had 6 loads total. I had some bulky blankets and a couple of pillows that needed washing too. What a day!

Anyway, everything smelled clean. I couldn't detect cat pee. Everything just smells lightly fresh. Not perfumed or weird like some bio cleaners. Everything looks clean. This can be used to wash anything, but I would only buy this for the intent to wash pet stuff. It seems to work. Hopefully the kitties can't smell their old urine and hopefully they are done with the pee-fest they engaged in. UGH!

If it really removes the scent of CAT PEE (so much stronger than dog pee), then everything else you may need it for while be taken care of. So far so good on my end. It has been 30 hours since I put the clean bedding etc back on, and no pee or smell of it that I can tell. Fingers crossed!

reviews.title: Cat Pee on Clothing is Awful
reviews.text:
I ordered this because my cat has been having "accidents" - unhappy about the new litter I had introduced to her box, she peed on both my jeans and a robe. I had put both in the laundry but even after a solid wash, she went ahead and peed on the same two items weeks later! I read that this is because the scent is very hard to get out - once a cat leaves her urine there, she'll return to it, thinking it's OK to do it again. I learned that, before washing your stained clothes, it's best to add some baking soda and vinegar first, to draw out the scent and then do the laundry.

Well, that's a lot of work, and so when I saw this detergent especially made for pet-related stains, I jumped at the chance to try it. I just washed my jeans and robe again with this stuff in the hope that she won't confuse those two items for a litter box again. If she does, I'll update this review. For now, I'm giving it a cautious positive review.

reviews.title: My son's dingy whites are white again
reviews.text:
I have an older Top loader Whirlpool washer that is at least 25 to 35 years old. I bought it second hand, and I love it compared to the fancy shmancy HE washers that fail to clean as well. It is also the largest capacity washer that Whirlpool has ever made for home use. I have used energy efficient machines many times before, because I used to run a cleaning business for over 10 years. One of the services I provided was laundry. I used a large variety as most of my customers could afford the the luxury of top of the line appliances. I also have used just about all the most popular brands of detergent on the market. If money were no object for me, I would say that Tide and Gain are among the best name brand detergents. However, I have had to pinch a lot of pennies through the years like a lot of folks. So unless Tide or Gain was on sale I suffered through generic brand after generic. My all time most favorite brand of detergent is Oxiclean's Detergent, not the powder pretreater. I am talking about the sleek blue bottle that I used to be able to find a Walmart. However, it has always been quite pricey comparable to pricerange of Tide and it is becoming harder to find.

So in a pinch after reading so many reviews of all the versions of Presto detergent, I decided to try Presto frangrance free brand since it was on sale. I figured I had nothing to lose at less than $7 a bottle. Though, admittedly, I was wary about using something that was free from perfume, because it is hard for me to imagine how a soap that has no scent that is also a generic could possibly get rid of my funky monkey boy's rank smelly feet smell out of his grimy filthy socks. Now, of course I am not saying I would take more perfume smell to cover up for a lack of clean, but still it was just hard to imagine that such a small measured amount could possibly handle the task at hand. I have tried so many other generics that did not work without dumping what seemed like half a container's worth in a single load. Okay I am exaggerating, but suffice it to say that anything generic claiming to be able to truly clean clothes at a premium quality strength fell short most of the time with exception of both Target and Great Value's generic versions of Gain or Tide. Both Target's and Great Value brand do a decent comparable job. I also have found Aldi's generic version of Gain to be decent. Although, I still tend to pour more in the washer than is normally recommended, mainly because I want to be extra sure I get clean and since I am using am old fashioned top loader that uses so much water it seems that of all the generics before my laundry required more soap than is recommended, despite the manufacturers' claims to be adequate for both older machines like mine and HE machines.

Back to Presto, I decided to give it a real test drive by followed the instructions exactly. Since I was washing an extra large size load with extra filth from funky monkey boy, I used 3/4 of the cap full.

To my amazement the same funky monkey boy's socks that were dingy reddish brown from his goofiness wearing his socks outside without shoes on are white again. Better still nearly of his socks and t-shirts and undies are bright white again. Usually I am lucky to get an earthy cream to ivory shade of white. These are actually bright white. Better still all the rank smell was completely eliminated. The clothes have no perfume smell obviously being the soap is frangrance free, but they actually smell clean! I did not bother to pretreat the clothes, which I normally prefer to do in order to get them this white again, but even with pretreating, I do not usually get such a bright white as I did today. So I suspect that had I let them soak in the Presto overnight in the washer the older more stained socks would have been even whiter. I will give this a try next time. Meanwhile, I am thrilled with the results. Imagine that! I am thrilled with laundry. Who would have thought that one up? LOL!

o I recommend Presto? Absolutely! It is worth every penny and I hope Amazon keeps selling it.
